title: Beth McHugh (JTBD EdTech strategist) — Incorruptible articulated 'what I've felt in EdTech through my own experiences over the years'
summary: Beth McHugh — Jobs-to-be-done Innovation Strategist for EdTech — publishes a 21-like reflection: brought in as a fractional Product leader, asked to build financial projections for a solution that hadn't been defined ('making shit up to give the board a good story'). Ries's framing named the gap she'd been feeling for years — between the stated mission and the incentives shaping what gets funded, renewed, and rewarded.
blockquote:
I'm reading Eric Ries' Incorruptible, and it has articulated so much of what I've felt in EdTech through my own experiences over the years.

One example of many was when I was brought in as a fractional Product leader to fill a gap until they hired a full time person. At first, I was inspired about how they talked about the opportunities and the inspiring mission.

Then I was asked to build financial projections for a solution we hadn't even defined. 🙃

There was no evidence behind the numbers. We were making shit up to give the board a good story.
